# Release-notes symbol waivers — symbols RELEASE_NOTES.md names that no
# longer resolve in the tree, enforced by
# scripts/check-release-notes-symbols.sh.
#
# WHAT IS ENFORCED AND WHAT IS REVIEWED. All three rules below were
# stated here and enforced by NOTHING until #779 -- a file of rules for
# a gate that exists because prose decays, in prose the gate never read.
# Three of the four are mechanical and now fail the build. The fourth
# cannot be, and pretending otherwise would turn a human judgement into
# a green tick:
#
#   ENFORCED  an entry belongs to a CATEGORY LINE (below), and the
#             category is printed beside the symbol on every pass.
#   ENFORCED  a waiver whose symbol resolves, or that these notes no
#             longer mention, is stale and fails. Unlike the vuln
#             allowlist -- which goes stale when a remote database
#             moves, and only warns -- a waiver here goes stale because
#             somebody edited THIS tree, in the pull request being
#             checked.
#   ENFORCED  a symbol in the CURRENT release section cannot be waived.
#   REVIEWED  whether the reason is a REASON. "Renamed" is a word, not
#             an argument. No parser can tell a decision from a shrug,
#             so a person reads this file and the gate says so rather
#             than simulating it.
#
# Rules, following .github/vuln-allowlist.txt:
#   - An entry requires a reason. No bare tokens. "The gate complained"
#     is a suppression, not a decision. The entry is introduced by a
#     CATEGORY LINE -- a comment beginning `HISTORICAL` or `EXTERNAL`
#     after one space -- and every token until the next non-token line
#     belongs to it. A blank `#` inside a reason does not end it.
#   - Two categories, and the reason must say which:
#       HISTORICAL — the symbol was real when the sentence was written
#                    and has since been renamed or removed. Name the
#                    commit that changed it. Frozen release sections
#                    describe the tree as it was; rewriting them would
#                    be falsifying history to satisfy a check.
#       EXTERNAL   — the symbol belongs to a dependency, not to us, so
#                    it will never resolve in a tracked *.go file.
#   - A CURRENT release section has no third category. If a symbol in
#     the section being written does not resolve, the prose is wrong and
#     the fix is to correct it, not to waive it.
#
# HISTORICAL — v0.5.0, line 3110. `LastIP` / `LastIPv6` were exported
#   fields on dhcpManager when v0.5.0 shipped (introduced by b95679c,
#   "Track latest IP from bound/renew"). 9c46e87 unexported them to
#   lastIP / lastIPv6 behind ipMu during the post-v0.5.3 concurrency
#   pass. Both fields still exist; only their case changed.
#
#   Worth recording why this pair is the reason the check strips
#   comments: `LastIP` matched a tracked .go file right up until it did,
#   on one code comment at dhcp_manager.go:1090. A resolver that reads
#   comments would have waived `LastIP` and flagged `LastIPv6` — two
#   different answers for one renamed pair.
LastIP
LastIPv6
#
# HISTORICAL — v0.5.3, lines 2947 and 2951. `AwaitNetNS` and
#   netns.GetFromPath were both removed by 79d4d2f, "open the sandbox
#   netns by fd, not by /proc path" (#695). The paragraph describes the
#   /proc-path era accurately; the replacement is awaitContainerNetNS.
#
#   `GetFromPath` is NO LONGER WAIVED and its line is deliberately gone.
#   The symbol resolves again: the route-death probe opens the container
#   namespace by its SANDBOX KEY to attach a netlink subscription, which
#   is a path the engine owns rather than a /proc path built from a pid,
#   so #695's rule is untouched by it. Product code still reaches the
#   namespace through awaitContainerNetNS. A waiver that cannot fire is a
#   hole -- it would sit silent on the day the symbol really did go away
#   -- so it is removed rather than kept for tidiness.
AwaitNetNS
#
# HISTORICAL — v0.6.0, line 2790. `tombstoneMu` was the mutex guarding
#   the tombstone read-modify-write path. 6463aaa extracted the
#   tombstone store and moved the locking rule inside it (#658).
tombstoneMu
#
# HISTORICAL — v0.6.0, line 2832, and this one is self-describing: the
#   sentence exists to record that util.ParseJSONBody was RENAMED to
#   ParseJSONOrErrorResponse, which is present in the tree today. The
#   old name has to appear for the sentence to mean anything.
ParseJSONBody
#
# EXTERNAL — "Changes vs. upstream", line 3292. NetworkInspectOptions is
#   a Docker API type (github.com/docker/docker/api/types), named in a
#   list of upstream API changes. It is not ours and will not resolve
#   here.
NetworkInspectOptions
